correctness.rationale: The shift yields stationarity: translating by t sends U to its fractional part after adding t and reindexes by the integer part, which preserves the displacement law even conditional on U. Sitewise Gaussian tails give local finiteness. For integer N, a hole requires a squared displacement sum over 0,…,N at least N³/12+O(N²), uniformly in U. Nonnegative correlations give a covariance norm at most Λ by absolute row sums; Gaussian diagonalization gives the stated determinant bound with dimension loss only O(N) at fixed ε. This gives the lower bound on −log V. Conversely the evacuation box forces the protected sites outside, and its center has squared norm N³/12+O(N²) and squared differences O(N²), including the central jump. With both ends zero, expanding the AR energy gives (1−ρ)² times the squared norm plus ρ times the squared differences. The bounded coordinate error changes this energy by O(N²); initial density, volume, and fixed shift restriction have at most O(N) log cost. Dividing by twice the innovation variance gives the matching N³/(24Λ). Conditional on the block and shift, both exterior chains have bounded means and variances, by stationarity and AR(1) reversibility. Entry thresholds grow at least as N+k−1 at distance k, so the sum of conditional tail probabilities is uniformly o(1); no exterior independence is needed. Positivity for all finite L follows by containment in a sufficiently large integer window with positive void probability. Strict inequality from one follows from the positive chance for a single Gaussian-displaced site to land in any positive-length window. Monotonicity gives real lengths and ρ=0 yields the independent constant without a singular step. The recorded exact-rational checks illustrate the algebra; the script was inspected, not run, and the infinite-volume assertion follows from the analytic bounds.
residual_risks: Remainders are pointwise for fixed σ>0 and 0≤ρ<1; no claim about negative correlations, joint parameter limits, or finer asymptotics was validated.

value.rationale: The rate for a stationary rare-event model is motivated before calculation by lattice void estimates and the gap between mixing bounds and iid logarithmic order. For a fixed positive correlation the result determines exactly how dependence changes the cost, replacing marginal variance by integrated covariance. The two sides require a displacement threshold and a path attaining its leading energy while all external sites are controlled. An exact coefficient in a simple correlated benchmark is useful for comparison with future dependent-field bounds; the independent specialization alone is not the contribution.
residual_risks: The interpretation as a long-run-variance cost is established only for this AR(1) family, not arbitrary Gaussian covariances or other windows.
